title: Design System: Zapp Account Portfolio Presentation

display.purpose: Opening argument and only the most important portfolio statement.

headline.purpose: Chapter theses with compact editorial line-height.

title.purpose: Evidence and decision headings inside structured groups.

body.purpose: Explanatory narrative held to a comfortable reading measure.

label.purpose: Controls, navigation status, metadata, captions, and provenance.

shadows.name: product-ambient
shadows.purpose: Primary light-theme lift for framed product devices.

shadows.name: surface-soft
shadows.purpose: Quiet lift for selected panels, miniature devices, and floating controls.

shadows.name: hero-object
shadows.purpose: Reserved for the opening product render.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Button hover, active feedback, and color changes.

motion.name: state-expressive
motion.purpose: Decision-row movement and short directional state changes.

motion.name: content-swap
motion.purpose: Screen fades and position resets when product states change.

motion.name: reveal-rise
motion.purpose: Short upward chapter reveal with 90ms and 160ms child staggering.

motion.name: hero-breathe
motion.purpose: Low-amplitude product presence after the hero arrives.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Near-instant fallback that removes reveal transforms and preserves all content.

narrative.overview:
The system feels like a senior product designer walking an interviewer through a live argument: crisp editorial framing establishes the point, then large product screens prove it. It is calm, precise, and product-led, with generous space that lets one decision land before the next begins.

Cool white and graphite surfaces carry most of the visual weight. A restrained Zapp blue supplies the single clear signal for emphasis, action, selection, and data. Material depth is quiet everywhere except the framed phones, where realistic edges, inset shading, and ambient shadow make the product feel present rather than pasted into a slide.

Motion behaves as product evidence. Short reveals establish sequence, state changes explain interaction, and genuine prototypes or inline animation are preferred when they clarify the work. Every essential idea remains visible without motion, and the reduced-motion fallback removes transforms and near-eliminates duration.
keyCharacteristics: Generous editorial hierarchy with one dominant idea per chapter
Large framed phones as the strongest material objects
Cool white and graphite neutrals with one restrained Zapp blue accent
Clear Helvetica Neue/system sans typography with compact, confident weights
Short purposeful reveals, live product states, and reduced-motion parity
Light and dark themes that preserve the same role hierarchy

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Zapp blue is reserved for action, active state, evidence, and decisive emphasis; its rarity is what gives it authority.

rules.name: The Role-Preserving Theme Rule
rules.body: Dark mode changes luminance and material values, not the hierarchy or meaning of a color role.

rules.name: The Senior Sans Rule
rules.body: Keep Helvetica Neue/system sans throughout; earn hierarchy through disciplined scale and spacing rather than introducing a display face.

rules.name: The Surface-Scope Rule
rules.body: Chapter compositions belong to this portfolio presentation; future product surfaces inherit the tokens, materials, and interaction behavior, not its task-local slide arrangements.

rules.name: The Product Proof Rule
rules.body: The strongest depth belongs to the product object; editorial containers remain tonal or softly lifted.

rules.name: The Nested Material Rule
rules.body: Device shell and screen radii must remain visibly distinct; flattening them into one card radius removes the sense of real hardware.

rules.name: The Purposeful State Rule
rules.body: Motion must reveal sequence or prove interaction: 180-420ms for controls and content swaps, 560-760ms for chapter reveals, and a single 1000ms hero arrival. Reduced motion removes transforms and reduces duration to 0.01ms.

dos: **Do** let large, framed product screens carry the strongest depth and visual emphasis.
**Do** use Zapp blue for primary action, selected state, evidence, and decisive data.
**Do** keep body copy near 60-68 characters per line and preserve generous chapter spacing.
**Do** use genuine product motion or live prototypes when they clarify a decision, with a complete reduced-motion fallback.
**Do** preserve color-role meaning and contrast when translating between light and dark themes.
donts: **Don't** introduce extra accent hues, decorative gradients, or bright status colors into the presentation system.
**Don't** make every panel float; most narrative structure should come from tonal layers and one-pixel rules.
**Don't** substitute a decorative display typeface for the established Helvetica Neue/system sans voice.
**Don't** shrink multi-column desktop arrangements onto mobile; restore reading order and retain only the most useful product proof.
**Don't** promote a chapter's one-off composition into a universal layout rule for other surfaces.
